headline: Slow grind: AI capex wobble, frontier defaults, bond-market nerves, and walls creeping higher

events: US expands Section 232 tariffs to semiconductors-adjacent goods and pharma inputs; EU adds safeguard duties on Chinese steel and EVs
Ukraine front freezes along an armed line after stalled talks; no settlement, sanctions stay
Fed cuts to ~3.25%, ECB holds near 2%; world growth ~2.8%
Senegal and Bolivia enter debt restructurings under a slow G20 Common Framework
Chinese exports rerouted via Vietnam, Mexico and Gulf hubs; rules-of-origin enforcement tightens
Hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply; AI-heavy equity indices fall ~20%, dragging US investment and wealth effects
World growth dips to ~2.3%; global unemployment peaks ~5.4% as white-collar hiring freezes
Divided outcome in US elections; tariff regime kept, deficit ~6.5% of GDP
Japanese super-long JGB yields spike; BoJ slows QT and buys selectively
Pakistan returns to the IMF after reserve squeeze; record South Asian heatwave
Modest recovery to ~2.7% as AI investment resumes at a steadier pace focused on inference and agents
US 10-year yield touches 5% on term-premium concerns; interest costs exceed defence spending
French fiscal standoff widens OAT spreads; ECB signals TPI but does not activate
Ethiopia-Eritrea border war erupts, displacing over a million people
US-EU spat over digital services taxes adds tit-for-tat tariffs; China-Taiwan blockade drills rattle shipping insurers
El Nino-linked crop failures push food prices up; G20 average inflation peaks ~3.9%, delaying rate cuts
Egypt forced into a reprofiling of domestic and external debt after Gulf support slows
Most 2030 NDC targets missed; renewables reach ~41% of power but coal persists in Asia
AI agents widespread in back-office work; ~28% of firms use AI in production
Youth protests over jobs and food prices in Kenya, Nigeria, Bangladesh and Peru
World growth ~2.6%; India ~6.5%, China ~3.8%, euro area ~1%
Global public debt crosses 100% of GDP; US ~134%
WTO dispute settlement still paralysed; trade increasingly runs through bilateral and bloc deals
Warming ~1.58C; first 1.5C-exceeding decade-average acknowledged by scientists
Incremental pension and housing-supply reforms in several OECD countries; no grand bargains

winners: India and connector economies (Vietnam, Mexico, Gulf states, Morocco)
Owners of AI and grid infrastructure, utilities and transmission builders
Defence contractors and holders of short-duration high-yield cash
losers: Indebted frontier economies in Africa and South Asia
Young graduates in entry-level white-collar work and renters in big cities
Small export-dependent manufacturers caught between blocs, and the euro-area periphery/France
bullets: The world never fell into a crisis but never escaped one: growth averaged ~2.6% with a 2028 AI-capex wobble as the closest thing to a recession.
Public debt crept past 100% of world GDP; bond vigilantes periodically tested the US, Japan and France without forcing reform.
Tariffs drifted higher and trade reorganised into US-aligned, China-centred and swing-state corridors, with connector economies taking the arbitrage.
AI reached roughly 31% of firms, raising productivity in software, finance and services modestly while thinning entry-level jobs (~30M displaced cumulatively).
Four sovereign debt crises (Senegal, Bolivia, Pakistan, Egypt) were handled slowly and piecemeal, deepening Global South distrust of Western institutions.
Climate policy lagged badly: renewables hit ~43% of power, but warming reached ~1.58C and heat and food shocks became annual events.
Trust in institutions slipped to ~34/100 and unrest rose to ~46/100, driven by youth unemployment, housing costs and food prices rather than one big revolt.
Ukraine stayed a frozen armed standoff, the Middle East simmered, and a new Horn of Africa war added to a record displaced population.
wildcard: A coordinated cyberattack in early 2030 blacked out parts of the Baltic and Polish grid for two days, prompting an EU grid-security fund but no wider escalation.
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Lagos evening, a young graduate in a co-working cafe runs a dozen AI agents for overseas clients on a solar-battery backup while the city grid flickers and a TV overhead shows another tariff announcement.
